name: Oshkosh Corp.
business: Builds aerial work platforms, telehandlers, fire and airport vehicles, refuse trucks and tactical defense vehicles for construction, municipal, airport and government customers worldwide.

events.what: Investor Day: 2028 targets of $13B to $14B revenue, 12% to 14% adjusted operating margin (200 to 400 bps expansion), $18 to $22 EPS; Defense renamed Transport, Steve Nordlund named to lead it
CFO appointed (external hire), effective BEFORE the 18-month window (cutoff 2025-04-01); prior CFO Michael Pack moved to President, Vocational
events.from: Joby Aviation (CFO and Treasurer); 20+ years at Ford (CFO North America, CFO Lincoln)

events.what: Director added, board 10 to 11, OUTSIDE window

next_event.source: No new Investor Day found in Baba corpus; management reiterates the June 2025 Investor Day 2028 targets each quarter (Pfeifer, doc 107417, 2026-07-28). Next is the Q3 2026 earnings call (date not in Baba); CFO said Q4 should be stronger than Q3.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is adjusted operating income margin of 12% to 14% in 2028 (midpoint 13% used), compared with VA consensus operating margin (VA FY2025 9.64% matches the company's 9.6% adjusted figure, so VA is on an adjusted basis). Segment targets: Access 14% to 16%, Vocational 16% to 18%.

statements.quote: Sure. And just to correct the number, so it's $13 billion-$14 billion in revenue and 12%-14% margin. So that's our 2028 target. Obviously, many of the initiatives you've heard us talk about are gradual and over time.
statements.speaker: Matt Field

statements.quote: I'll finish with we laid out our targets to 2028 last year. We said we'll grow to $13 billion-$14 billion in revenue. We'll increase our operating margins by 200-400 basis points. That would take it to 12%-14% at the highest level. We will deliver $18-$22 per share
statements.speaker: John Pfeifer

statements.quote: As a result of our revised expectations for production this year, we now expect full-year adjusted earnings per share in the range of $11.
statements.speaker: John Pfeifer

statements.quote: To reiterate, we remain confident in our plans to achieve our 2028 financial targets.
statements.speaker: John Pfeifer

street.gap_assumption: December year end, Baba FY labels equal calendar years. Compares the 13% midpoint of the 12% to 14% 2028 adjusted operating margin target with VA FY2028 consensus operating margin 11.31% (consensus operating margin path 9.31% / 10.61% / 11.31% for FY2026 to FY2028). Against the 12% low end the gap is 69 bps. Street FY2028 revenue $12.69B is below the $13B to $14B target. EBITDA uplift assumes flat D&A.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (fundamentals, Visible Alpha, fetched 2026-10-01)

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adjusted operating margin. Q1 2026 4.15% vs 8.29% (VA). Q2 2026 adjusted operating income $258M on sales $2,915M (Q2 2025 $2,732M plus $183M, Field, doc 107417) = 8.85% vs 11.45%. 2026 EPS guide cut to about $11 on slower fire-truck throughput. LTM adjusted operating margin Q3 2025 to Q2 2026 is 8.05%; LTM EBITDA margin (VA, Q2 2025 to Q1 2026) is 10.9%. Margins are moving away from the target, not toward it.

verdict: Best numeric framing of the four (dated 12% to 14% 2028 margin, reiterated by CEO and CFO) and a 169 bps gap to a stabilized street, but no fresh leadership catalyst: CEO 5.5 years in, CFO change outside the window.
open_questions: Can fire-truck throughput and NGDV ramp lift adjusted operating margin from about 8% LTM to 12% to 14% in two years, or is the target reset at the next framework update?
How much of the 169 bps gap is Access cyclicality (11.3% vs 14% to 16% target) versus Vocational and Transport execution?
Is there a pending leadership change or new Investor Day that would re-underwrite the 2028 targets?
